items.title: Section: What Must Be Relinquished, What Distorts, and What Alone Can See the Fault

items.zh: 問：幾根於義雜染捨所顯？答：除諸善根，以諸善根於義清淨捨所顯故。問：幾根顛倒義？答：除諸善根，所有六根義。問：幾根顛倒所依？答：七色根。問：幾根顛倒自性？答：六少分。問：幾根顛倒對治？答：八物。問：幾根觀義過失？答：或八、或五、或一。
items.en: Question: how many faculties are manifested by the relinquishing of defilement? Answer: excepting the wholesome faculties, since the wholesome faculties are manifested instead by the relinquishing of purity's own object. Question: how many are subsumed under distortion's meaning? Answer: excepting the wholesome faculties, the object belonging to six faculties. Question: how many serve as distortion's supporting basis? Answer: the seven form faculties. Question: how many constitute distortion's very essence? Answer: a portion of six. Question: how many serve as the antidote to distortion? Answer: eight faculties. Question: how many can observe the fault in conditioned existence? Answer: either eight, or five, or one.

items.title: Section: Four Virtues Non-Buddhists Claim for Conditioned Existence, and Why None of Them Hold

items.zh: 問：若彼諸行亦有四德相應可得，云何唯觀為過失耶？何者四德？一、堅住德；謂如一蘊住經百年，若正將御，或有過者。二、勢力德；謂能生樂，及現清淨。三、轉變德；謂牽引、修治、受用、棄捨自在轉故。四、可樂德；謂依彼處生種種著故。是名諸行有四德相。答：雖有世間於彼諸法取為功德，然彼一切皆諸過失之所隨逐。問：何等名為諸過失耶？
items.en: Question: if conditioned formations also possess four qualities that can genuinely be found in them, why observe only fault? What are the four qualities? First, an enduring quality: a single aggregate can persist for a hundred years if properly cared for, or fail earlier through mismanagement. Second, a powerful quality: it can generate pleasure and manifest present purity. Third, a transformative quality: it can be drawn along, cultivated, employed, and discarded, freely operating at will. Fourth, a desirable quality: it gives rise to all manner of attachment depending on the circumstance relied upon. These are called the four qualities of conditioned formations. Answer: although the world takes these to be genuine virtues, every one of them is thoroughly accompanied by fault. Question: what, then, are called the faults?

items.title: Section: Why Even Dung Beetles Enjoy What They Enjoy — Refuting the Four Claimed Virtues

items.zh: 答：雖少時住，非究竟故，愛變無常現可得故，死沒無常現可得故，當觀諸行離初功德。又能發生種種苦惱現可得故，種種不淨現可得故，當觀諸行離第二德。又於老病死等不隨所欲現可得故，當觀諸行離第三德。又諸糞蟲及猪犬等亦極樂著糞穢不淨現可得故，當觀諸行離第四德。由彼諸行離諸功德，是故一切過失相應，故應觀彼具諸過失。問：眼根誰所依處？答：見色依處。問：乃至意根誰所依處？答：各取自境之所依處。
items.en: Answer: although persisting a short while, it is never ultimately enduring, since the transformation of what is cherished, and the inevitability of death, are both directly observable — conditioned formations should be seen as lacking the first virtue. It also gives rise to every variety of suffering and impurity, directly observable — conditioned formations should be seen as lacking the second virtue. Old age, sickness, and death do not yield to one's own wishes, directly observable — conditioned formations should be seen as lacking the third virtue. Dung beetles, pigs, and dogs likewise take the greatest delight in filth and impurity, directly observable — conditioned formations should be seen as lacking the fourth virtue. Since conditioned formations lack these virtues, they are accompanied by fault in every respect, and should therefore be observed as possessing every fault. Question: what does the eye faculty serve as the basis for? Answer: the basis for seeing form. Question: down to the mind faculty, what does each serve as the basis for? Answer: each serves as the basis for engaging its own respective object.

items.title: Section: The Lamp in a Windless Room — What Each Faculty Actually Grounds

items.zh: 問：男女二根誰所依處？答：習欲依處。問：命根誰所依處？答：乃至死有，為前時有之所依處。問：諸受根誰所依處？答：於諸境界可意、不可意，若愛、若恚等之所依處。問：信根誰所依處？答：趣入善法之所依處。問：精進根誰所依處？答：已入善法，恒常修習之所依處。問：念根誰所依處？答：正知而行之所依處。問：定根誰所依處？答：智見清淨之所依處。問：慧根誰所依處？答：煩惱永斷之所依處。問：未知欲知根誰所依處？答：證初、第二、第三沙門果之所依處。
items.en: Question: what do the male and female faculties serve as the basis for? Answer: the basis for engaging in desire. Question: what does the life faculty serve as the basis for? Answer: existence prior to the moment of death. Question: what do the faculties of feeling serve as the basis for? Answer: craving or aversion towards pleasant or unpleasant objects. Question: what does the faith faculty serve as the basis for? Answer: entering wholesome practice. Question: what does the diligence faculty serve as the basis for? Answer: sustaining wholesome practice once entered. Question: what does the mindfulness faculty serve as the basis for? Answer: acting with clear comprehension. Question: what does the concentration faculty serve as the basis for? Answer: purifying wisdom and insight. Question: what does the wisdom faculty serve as the basis for? Answer: permanently severing affliction. Question: what does the aspirant's faculty serve as the basis for? Answer: attaining the first, second, or third fruit of the contemplative life.

items.title: Section: Seventeen Ways to See Through the Body — Scripture Explained Through the Faculties

items.zh: 問：已知根誰所依處？答：乃至金剛喻定、無學沙門果證之所依處。問：具知根誰所依處？答：無間煩惱永斷作證、現法樂住、所依永滅之所依處。問：世尊依何根處說如是言：此身有色，麁滓所成，四大所造，父母不淨和合所生，種種飲食之所長養，常假覆蔽、沐浴、按摩、斷截、破壞、散、滅之法？答：依七色根作如是說。
items.en: Question: what does the knower's faculty serve as the basis for? Answer: everything up through the vajra-like concentration and the realisation of the fruit beyond training. Question: what does the faculty of complete knowledge serve as the basis for? Answer: the uninterrupted, permanent severing of affliction actually realised, dwelling in bliss in this very life, and the permanent cessation of what one depends upon. Question: on what faculty's basis did the Blessed One speak these words: this body is made of form, composed of coarse remnants, built from the four great elements, born from the impure union of parents, sustained by various foods, constantly requiring covering, bathing, and massage, and subject to being cut, broken, dispersed, and destroyed? Answer: he spoke resting on the seven physical faculties.

items.zh: 當知此中，略說欲界有色諸根。初句說彼共相。第二句說彼自相。次有三句說彼因相。所謂依因、生因、生已增長因。次有三句說彼轉變相。謂寒所作、熱所作、勞倦所作。後有四句說彼變壞相。謂初二句活位逼損所作，後二句死後所作；他故、自然故變壞應知。

items.title: Section: The Mind That Travels Far, Travels Alone, and Dwells Bodiless in Its Own Cave

items.zh: 問：世尊依何根處說如是言：遠行及濁行，無身寢於窟耶？答：依意根處。由於前際無始時故，遍緣一切所知境故，名為遠行。
items.en: Question: on what faculty's basis did the Blessed One speak these words: travelling far and travelling alone, bodiless, dwelling within a cave? Answer: resting on the mind faculty. Because it comes from the beginningless past, and ranges over every knowable object, it is called far-travelling.

items.title: Section: No One Is Driving — Why Mind Has No Ruler, and the Eight Ways Attraction Binds

items.zh: 諸心相續一一轉故，無主宰故，名為獨行。無色、無見亦無對故，名為無身。依止色故，名寢於窟。問：依何根處說如是言：由八處所男為女縛，謂舞、歌、笑、睇、美顏、妙觸、祇奉、成禮？答：依男女二根。於遊戲時，由四處縛；於受用時，亦由四處。
items.en: Because each moment of mind arises one at a time in succession, with no ruling master, it is called alone-travelling. Because it has no form, no visibility, and no resistance, it is called bodiless. Because it depends on the body, it is called dwelling in a cave. Question: on what basis did the Blessed One speak of eight things by which a man becomes bound to a woman — dance, song, laughter, a glance, beauty of countenance, delightful touch, attentive service, and the completion of marriage? Answer: resting on the male and female faculties. Four bind during playful courtship; the same four bind during actual enjoyment as well.

items.zh: 於遊戲時，身、語、面門、眼目舒悅；於受用時，妍容、軟滑、恭事、童分。

blocks.text: Non-Buddhists praise conditioned existence for four "virtues". The treatise answers each, and then explains a famous verse about the mind.
Master Cháng Bǎi: a portion of six faculties joined with greed, hatred, and delusion is the essence of distortion.
Endurance ("properly cared for, an aggregate lasts a hundred years or more"), power, transformation, and purity. Master Cháng Bǎi: they match permanence, bliss, self, and purity.

Master Cháng Bǎi: from impermanence one knows conditioned things lack endurance; they do not keep beings happy but bring suffering. Even dung beetles delight in dung; delight proves nothing about purity.
Faith enters, diligence sustains, mindfulness acts with clear comprehension, concentration purifies knowledge and vision, and wisdom severs.

Master Cháng Bǎi: "dwelling in bliss in this life" is nirvāṇa with remainder; "cessation of the support" is nirvāṇa without remainder. (Untranslated, 0617a06: the structure of the sūtra's phrases about the body: its shared mark, its own mark, its causes, its changes through cold, heat, and fatigue, and its decay in life and after death.)
Master Cháng Bǎi: minds appear one by one, moment by moment, with no one there as master; this is "travelling alone".
Eight bonds of attraction: dance, song, laughter, glance, beauty, touch, service, and rite.
"No one there as master." The verse describes the mind's freedom and its loneliness at once.

quiz.q: How does the lecture explain the essence of distortion and those observing fault?
options: the seven physical faculties are distortion's essence; five are the feelings, one is life, which sees the fault of saṃsāra
a portion of six joined with greed, hatred, and delusion; five are faith and the rest, one is mind, where practice begins
eight are distortion's essence; five are the sense faculties
distortion has no essence, so the question fails
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a portion of these six joined with greed, hatred, and delusion is called distortion's essence. Five speaks of real phenomena, faith and the rest; one speaks of the chief, the mind. Practice begins with mind: on it arises the consciousness that sees fault in conditioned things and turns away. The English "fault in conditioned existence" expands 義 here.

quiz.q: The English has "or fail earlier through mismanagement." Is this right?
options: no: 或有過者 is going beyond a hundred; the lecture says a hundred years or even more; the English reverses it
yes: 過 means fault, and mismanaged it fails early, the opposite of endurance, so the English agrees with the lecture
no: it should read "and pass on to others"
no: the Chinese speaks of a hundred eons
quiz.why: The clause praises endurance: properly cared for, an aggregate lasts a hundred years or even longer. Master Cháng Bǎi reads it as abiding a hundred years, or even exceeding that. 過 here means exceeding, not fault. The English "fail earlier through mismanagement" adds a failure the Chinese does not state and undoes the point of the quality.

quiz.q: How do the four qualities match permanence, bliss, self, and purity?
options: endurance to permanence, power to bliss, transformation to self, desirability to purity
endurance to self, power to permanence, transformation to purity, desirability to bliss
endurance to bliss, power to purity, transformation to permanence, desirability to self
all four to permanence
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: these four excellent qualities match permanence, bliss, self, and purity in order. Power is taken as the ability to give pleasure; transformation is what outsiders take as a self drawing the body along. The English rendering as "qualities" is neutral, while the treatise is reporting a worldly view.

quiz.q: How does the treatise refute endurance and power?
options: the change of what is cherished and death refute endurance; suffering and impurity refute power
old age and death not obeying wishes refute endurance; dung beetles and pigs refute power
brief duration refutes power; suffering refutes endurance
the treatise does not refute them
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: from the various kinds of impermanence one knows all conditioned things lack endurance; there is no power as outsiders claim, since they do not keep beings happy but constantly produce suffering and impurity. Old age and sickness refute the third quality; dung beetles the fourth.

quiz.q: The English has "Dung beetles" for 糞蟲. Is this good, and what does the example refute?
options: best: 糞蟲 are beetles, and the example refutes power, since beetles push loads heavier than themselves, showing conditioned things lack any strength worth prizing
it should be "flies"; it refutes endurance
糞蟲 means maggots and such, "dung beetles" being narrow; it refutes desirability: delight does not prove purity
it should be "worms"; it refutes transformation
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: in this way one should observe that all conditioned things are impure, without the purity outsiders claim. Since even creatures delight in filth, delight proves nothing about purity. 糞蟲 is a general term for creatures living in dung, such as maggots, which the English narrows to one insect.

quiz.q: Of what are the faculties of faith, diligence, concentration, and wisdom each the basis?
options: severing affliction; purity of knowledge; constant cultivation; entering the wholesome, practice beginning from severing
clear comprehension; entering the wholesome; severing; purity
all are bases of desire
entering the wholesome; constant cultivation once entered; purity of knowledge and vision; severing affliction permanently
quiz.why: The treatise's order is a path: faith enters, diligence sustains, mindfulness acts with clear comprehension, concentration purifies knowledge and vision, and wisdom severs. Master Cháng Bǎi: only after believing can one enter the wholesome, then one must cultivate constantly; concentration alone cannot sever afflictions, which requires wisdom.

quiz.q: What do the knower's faculty and complete knowledge support, and how do bliss here and cessation differ?
options: the knower's: the first three fruits; complete: entering the wholesome; bliss is without remainder, cessation with
both rest on the vajra-like concentration; no difference
neither is a basis
the knower's: up to the vajra-like concentration and adept fruit; complete: realised severing and so on; bliss here is with remainder, cessation without
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: dwelling in bliss in this life means the adept has realised nirvāṇa with remainder, and cessation of the support means entering nirvāṇa without remainder. The first three fruits belong to the aspirant's faculty. The English "what one depends upon" could use a clearer reference to the body.

quiz.q: On which faculty rests the verse on travelling far and alone, and how are its four phrases explained?
options: mind: beginningless and all-ranging is far; successive and masterless is alone; formless is bodiless; relying on form is the cave
life: long life is far; dying alone is alone; the intermediate state is bodiless; the womb is the cave
the seven physical: going far
faith: faith reaching far
quiz.why: The treatise rests the verse on the mind faculty. Master Cháng Bǎi: minds appear one by one, moment by moment, with no one there as master, and this is travelling alone. The verse is a classic statement that mind has no ruler and can therefore be trained.

quiz.q: The English has "the same four bind during actual enjoyment." Is this right?
options: no: the eight divide into two different groups of four; 亦由四處 does not mean the same four
yes: 亦 means the same, the eight being really four, dance, song, laughter, and glance in both
no: it should read five
no: the Chinese lacks 受用
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi matches dance, song, laughter, and glance to play. The other four, beauty, touch, service, and rite, belong to enjoyment. Since eight are listed and split into two groups, 亦 means likewise four, not the identical four. The English "the same four" collapses eight into four.
